Item No. 2
                  Committee Staff Summary for September 10, 2026 WRC


2.       Private Lands Management Program

Today’s Item                             Information ☐                      Action ☒
Receive and discuss Department recommended regulatory amendments, and develop
potential recommendation related to private lands wildlife habitat enhancement and
management licenses and plans.

Summary of Previous/Future Actions
                             Action                                            Date

     •   Initial vetting                                         May 14, 2026; WRC
     •   Today’s discussion and potential                        September 10, 2026; WRC
         recommendation
     •   Present recommendations to the Commission               October 13-16, 2026

Background
The Private Lands Management (PLM) Program, administered by the Department, encourages
private property owners within California to develop and implement wildlife habitat
enhancement and management plans that actively encourage the propagation, conservation
and wise use of the fish and wildlife species on their property, as well as to protect and
enhance wildlife habitat.

Pursuant to California Fish and Game Code Section 3400 et seq, and California Code of
Regulations, Title 14, Section 601, applicants develop a management plan that is reviewed
and approved by the Department, after which the Commission may approve the plan and grant
a license for a period of five years. Each licensee is required to submit an annual report to the
Department documenting that various requirements have been met, after which the
Department provides the Commission with a recommendation for each license and whether it
should be continued.

Currently, the PLM Program protects over one-million acres of habitat statewide.

Updates
On August 19, 2026, the Department held a meeting with PLM licensees and stakeholders to
discuss the Department’s recommendations to the Wildlife Resources Committee (WRC). The

Significant Public Comments
A PLM operator from Monterey County extolls the PLM Program, agrees that the Department
needs access to PLM properties and that the PLM Program should foster more access to
hunting opportunities for the public. He disagrees that PLM hunters should be limited to one
tag because it may discourage hunters from spending money in California. (Exhibit 2)

Recommendation
Commission staff: Recommend the Commission support a future rulemaking regarding the
PLM Program, based on today’s discussion.
Department: Support a future rulemaking regarding the PLM Program, as recommended.

Exhibits
   1.    Department presentation
   2.    Email from Doug Roth, received August 24, 2026

Committee Direction/Recommendation
The Wildlife Resources Committee recommends that the Commission support a future
rulemaking regarding the PLM Program, based on the Department’s recommendation and
today’s discussion.

3.       Annual Regulation Changes

Today’s Item                             Information ☐                     Action ☒
Receive and discuss Department recommended regulatory amendments, and develop
potential recommendations, for 2027-28 seasons related to:
(A) Waterfowl hunting
(B) Central Valley sport fishing
(C) Klamath River Basin sport fishing

Summary of Previous/Future Actions
                            Action                                         Date

     •   Initial vetting                                      May 14, 2026; WRC
     •   Today’s discussion and potential                     September 10, 2026; WRC
         recommendations
     •   Present recommendations to the Commission            October 13-16, 2026

Background
This item provides the public an opportunity to engage in discussions with the Wildlife
Resources Committee (WRC) and Department about potential regulation changes for waterfowl
hunting, Central Valley sport fishing, and Klamath River sport fishing.

Waterfowl Hunting (2027-28)
Annually, the Commission amends waterfowl hunting regulations to conform State regulations
with federal regulations. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service adopts federal regulations each
October based, in part, on recommendations from four regional flyway councils. Migratory
waterfowl include American coot, common moorhen, ducks, black brant, and geese, among
others.

Central Valley Sport Fishing (2028)
The Commission adopts Central Valley sport fishing regulations on an annual basis to align
State regulations with federal regulations for the American, Feather, Sacramento and
Mokelumne rivers. The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) adopts federal Central
Valley salmon escapement goals each April based, in large part, on recommendations from

Author: Ari Cornman                                                                            1

Item No. 3
                  Committee Staff Summary for September 10, 2026 WRC

PFMC, after which the Department proposes State regulation changes based upon those
allocations and the status of the stock.

PFMC does not make recommendations for Klamath River Basin spring-run Chinook salmon;
beginning last year (2025), the Department makes recommendations for Klamath River Basin
spring-run Chinook salmon seasons and bag and possession limits based on stock status,
environmental conditions, and fisheries management outcomes for the Klamath River Basin
fall-run Chinook salmon fishery.

Today, the Department will present its proposed regulatory options for Klamath River Basin
2027 spring-run and fall-run Chinook salmon fisheries (Exhibit 2).

Today’s Meeting
This meeting is an opportunity for interested parties to make suggestions to WRC regarding
potential regulation changes for each of the three topics. WRC may make recommendations to
the Commission for consideration for each rulemaking.

Significant Public Comments (N/A)

Recommendation
Commission staff: Recommend the Commission support future rulemakings regarding
waterfowl hunting, Central Valley sport fishing, and Klamath River Basin sport fishing, based
on today’s discussion.
Department: Support future rulemakings regarding waterfowl hunting, Central Valley sport
fishing, and Klamath River Basin sport fishing, as recommended.

Exhibits
   1.    Department presentation, Central Valley sport fishing
   2.    Department presentation, Klamath River Basin sport fishing

Committee Direction/Recommendation
The Wildlife Resources Committee recommends that the Commission support future
rulemakings regarding waterfowl hunting, Central Valley sport fishing, and Klamath River Basin
sport fishing, based on the Department’s recommendations and today’s discussion.

4.     Periodic Regulation Changes

Today’s Item                             Information ☐                      Action ☒
Receive and discuss Department recommended regulatory amendments, and develop
potential recommendations, for 2027-28 seasons related to:
(A) Upland (resident) game bird hunting
(B) Big game hunting
         I.     Deer
         II.    Elk
         III.   Bighorn sheep
         IV.    Pronghorn antelope
         V.     Black bear

Summary of Previous/Future Actions
                             Action                                            Date

 •   Initial vetting                                             May 14, 2026; WRC
 •   Today’s discussion and potential                            September 10, 2026; WRC
     recommendation
 •   Present any recommendations to the Commission               October 13-16, 2026

Background
When amendments to regulations are regularly sought for a particular subject (e.g., deer
hunting), but are not required every year, they are referred to as “periodic” rulemakings. This
item is an opportunity to engage in initial discussions with the Wildlife Resources Committee
(WRC), staff, and Department staff about recommended regulation changes for periodic
rulemakings.

(A) Upland (Resident) Game Bird Hunting (2027-28)
     Resident upland game bird species include, among others, California quail, pheasant,
     wild turkey, chukar, and Eurasian collared-dove. Greater sage-grouse is also a resident
     game bird, though hunting has been disallowed since June of 2023 when it was declared
     a candidate species under the California Endangered Species Act.

Author: Ari Cornman                                                                               1

     Seasons, quotas, bag and possession limits, hunt zones, Shared Habitat Alliance for
     Recreational Enhancement (SHARE) Program tags, the tag drawing system, disease
     management, etc. are defined for each species in sections 351 through 367.5, sections
     554 through 555.1, and sections 708.1 through 708.19.

This meeting is an opportunity for interested parties to make suggestions to WRC and the
Department regarding potential regulation changes for each of the six subjects identified under
this agenda topic.

Today’s Meeting
Today, the Department will present recommendations for rulemakings, including new
recommendations for deer hunting (Exhibit 1) and updated concepts for elk hunting (Exhibit 2).
Discussion will continue on the other subjects, including previous recommendations for bighorn
sheep (Exhibit 3) and black bear (Exhibit 4). WRC potentially will develop recommendations for
the Commission to consider in the context of potential rulemakings.

Significant Public Comments (N/A)

Recommendation
Commission staff: Recommend the Commission support future rulemakings related to deer,
elk, bighorn sheep, and black bear hunting, based on today’s discussion.
Department: Support future rulemakings regarding deer, elk, bighorn sheep, and black bear
hunting, as recommended.

Exhibits
   1.      Department presentation for deer
   2.      Department presentation for elk
   3.      Department presentation for bighorn sheep
   4.      Department presentation for black bear

Committee Direction/Recommendation
The Wildlife Resources Committee recommends that the Commission support future
rulemaking related to deer, elk, bighorn sheep, and black bear hunting, based on the
Department’s recommendation and today’s discussion.

5.        Inland Sport Fishing

Today’s Item                               Information ☒                     Action ☐
Receive and discuss Department recommended regulatory amendments related to inland
sport fishing.

Summary of Previous/Future Actions
                               Action                                             Date

 •       Today’s initial vetting                                 September 10, 2026; WRC
 •       Discussion and potential recommendation                 January 13, 2027; WRC
 •       Present recommendation to the Commission                February 10-11, 2027

Background
Annually, the Department presents to WRC recommendations for changes to inland sport
fishing regulations; when recommended changes are not urgently necessary, they may be held
to combine with future recommendations.

Today, the Department will present and discuss its initial recommendations for changes to
sport fishing regulations, suggested to become effective in January 2028. Initial
recommendations include:
     •    Barrett Reservoir (also known as Barrett Lake) special regulation removal for black bass
          to simplify the regulation and increase opportunity
     •    Silver Creek (Mono County) opening for trout catch-and-release
     •    Seasonal closure of the Middle Fork Eel River to protect summer steelhead and
          increase consistency with other forks of the Eel River
     •    Removal of Sespe Creek from Trout Waters with Special Fishing Regulations due to the
          determination of the mainstem as anadromous waters for southern California steelhead
     •    Seasonal closure of the Eel River 1000 feet above and below the Van Duzen mouth to
          protect Chinook salmon
     •    South Central Coast District steelhead season adjustment to correct misalignment with
          peak steelhead run
